people.gloss: The bamboo seed the phoenix eats (Trang Tử)
people.role: Head of Trúc Thực Viên since 1050; the spirit farmer who makes the bamboo seed every year
people.appearance: A broad, slow man with mud dried grey to the knee, a straw hat on his back and a red clay censer hung from his belt like a lantern.
people.backstory: Ninh Trúc Thực was born in the garden in 900 to a seed-picker, with a Fire the wet bamboo land almost never breeds. The second head Tất Mạn Thu (tat_man_thu) took him at ten because he could warm a cold seedbed with his hands. In 990 he watched the whole grove flower, seed and die in a month, as bamboo does once in sixty years, and he watched the bamboo rats come down from Trúc Thử Nguyên to eat the fallen seed and then the villages' rice. In 1050 the grove flowered again, Tất died with it (N-truc_thuc-03), and he became head. That spring he lit a censer at the foot of the young clumps and walked the rows with it for nine nights, and they seeded. They have seeded every year since (A246). The palace's birds, Bách Vũ's messengers and the spirit fields of Điền Phong Niên (dien_phong_nien) now eat that seed every year, and the garden's name has never stood higher. He trades with Điền every autumn and gives away more than he sells. He has trained eleven disciples and none of them has Fire.
people.wants: To find one disciple who can carry the censer into the grove after him.
people.secret: He has not bred a new bamboo. It is the old sixty-year grove, forced to seed every spring by his Fire. When he stops, every clump will flower at once and die, and the rats will come as they did in 990, but worse, because they have been breeding on the yearly seed for 150 years.

people.role: Elder of the Water Fields (Thủy Điền), the flood terraces below the grove; keeper of the garden's rain record
people.appearance: A lean, sun-dark woman with her trousers rolled to the thigh and a gourd at her hip, who looks at the sky before she looks at anyone.
people.backstory: Úy Thương Điền is a fisher's daughter from Bích Lãng Thôn, where the jade waves carry the boats home (A244). The garden took her in 1026 on her Wood, and she found that her Water was the stronger. In 1108 she cut the first flood terraces below the grove and wrote the Flooded Field Verse as a work song, and since then half the garden's people have been the Water-rooted children of the coast villages, whom the palace would never take. She has measured every rain since in a gourd and written the numbers in a book. The book says that the land under the grove dries a little more every decade, and the bamboo rats on Trúc Thử Nguyên have doubled since 1150. She has asked Ninh Trúc Thực (ninh_truc_thuc) four times to let the grove rest one year. Four times he has said no and has not told her why. She is the reason the garden now writes its lineage as Wood and Water (N-truc_thuc-05).
people.wants: One fallow year for the grove, before the land and the rats decide it for them.
people.secret: Since 1150 she has kept a second grove at Tử Trúc Lâm, grown from old sixty-year seed she saved before 1050, against the day the head's grove fails. Planting it says she expects him to fail, so she has never told him.

people.role: The head's true disciple and expected heir; runs the seed harvest
people.appearance: Quiet, with green-stained fingers, he stands with his weight on one leg like a heron.
people.backstory: Born in the garden in 1090 and given to Ninh Trúc Thực (ninh_truc_thuc) at six, Mẫn Tiết Thanh has learned every row, every rain and every seed count the head knows. He runs the harvest that goes up to the palace each autumn. He has asked twice to carry the censer into the grove in spring, and twice the head has held it a moment and then taken it back. He thinks he has failed a test. He has no Fire, and no one has told him that is the whole of it.
people.wants: The censer in his own hands one spring, and to learn what test he failed.
people.secret: Nights, he warms a seedbed in the lower rows with hot kitchen bricks, trying to seed bamboo without Fire; three rows have sprouted, and Ứng Sơ Hoa, who carries his knives, has seen the ash.

people.role: Rat warden of Trúc Thử Nguyên, the bamboo rats' plain three tiles from the garden
people.appearance: Wiry and homely in a rat-skin cloak, missing the tip of his nose to a bamboo rat the size of a dog.
people.backstory: A raft-maker's son from Trúc Phiệt Thôn, Khuất Liệp Nguyên has lived on Trúc Thử Nguyên since 1140 and keeps the garden's fences against the bamboo rats. He sells their pelts at Bích Lãng and their meat to Bách Vũ Các for its hawks. He counts them every winter and gives the count to Úy Thương Điền (uy_thuong_dien), because the head only nods. There were nine hundred in 1150; this winter he stopped counting at four thousand. Last month he found their runs under the brook toward Bích Lãng's paddies. He has begun to sell hawks' meat by the sack, and a bigger count is a bigger sack.
people.wants: A count of rats the head must answer to, and the hawk-keeper's debt cleared by spring.
people.secret: He is not culling the northern runs: the hawk-keeper of Bách Vũ pays by the sack, so he hands Úy Thương Điền the alarming count and keeps the rats fat.

people.role: Carries the seed tribute to Hoàng Vân Thành and the Wutong Court each autumn
people.appearance: A tidy woman in a blue travelling coat, always smelling of cooked rice, who knows everyone's name at the granary gate.
people.backstory: A grain-broker's daughter from Mạch Điền Trấn, Sầm Đạo Hương joined the garden for its Water fields and stayed for its roads. Every autumn she drives the seed carts to Điền Phong Niên (dien_phong_nien) at Hoàng Vân Thành and then up the ridge to Vu Ngô Đồng's aviary (vu_ngo_dong). She drinks with the palace's healer Từ Cam Tuyền (tu_cam_tuyen) and hears everything first. She would like a seat in the palace's Hall of Benevolence and knows that a Fire root is the price. She tells the palace what it likes to hear, and is paid for it.
people.wants: A seat in the Hall of Benevolence, and to be the one the palace hears the garden's news from.
people.secret: She has told Từ Cam Tuyền at the palace that the head's seed will fail, and is selling the rest of the story one cart at a time to find what the palace will pay to hear it first.

He sells the lower rows' second picking to the carters as a steward's due, and docks Chu Thu Điền (chu_thu_dien), who works the rows, the share that should have been his.

people.role: Founder of Trúc Thực Viên (760); a palace outer disciple who never passed the Feather Kindling
people.backstory: A Wood-rooted peach farmer's son from Đào Khê who sat the palace's Feather Kindling forty-one times and never held the feather without burning. In 760 he led forty other unkindled outer disciples down to the wet grass below Tử Trúc Lâm and asked the palace for one thing: leave to grow the bamboo seed the phoenix eats (A243, N-truc_thuc-01). The palace gave it, with sixty years of rice. He lived to see the flowerings of 810 and 870.

people.role: Second head of Trúc Thực Viên (905-1050); wrote the Sixty-Year Flower
people.backstory: The founder Ông Lục Tiết's (ong_luc_tiet) last disciple, garden-born, head from 905. After the flowering of 990 she wrote the Sixty-Year Flower from what she watched the bamboo do.
